summary: Friedrich Carl von Savigny worked in history and archaeology and other fields. He studied at the universities of Marburg, Jena, and Leipzig. He later held posts at the University of Marburg (~1800–1804) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1842).

Friedrich Christian Charles Augustus Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Augustenburg was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Heidelberg University (~1850–1852), Trinity College, Cambridge (1852), and the University of Paris, learning under Theodor Goldstücker.

Friedrich Christian Diez was a linguist who studied at the University of Giessen (~1811–1813) under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and at the University of Göttingen (~1813–1814). He held a post at the University of Bonn from ~1823 to 1876.

Friedrich Creuzer was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Tübingen and Jena, and later held posts at Marburg (~1800–1804), Heidelberg (~1804–1845), and Leiden (1809).

Friedrich Delitzsch studied linguistics and history at Leipzig, Berlin, and Jena under Brockhaus, Windisch, Weber, Fleischer, Dillmann, Schrader, and Curtius. He served as professor at Leipzig (1877), Breslau (1893), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1899).
Friedrich Ernst August Krause was a sinologist who studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen. He later held an academic post at Heidelberg University from approximately 1923 to 1942.

Linguist Friedrich Ernst Kieckers studied at Bonn, Munich, Marburg, Berlin, and Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen. He held posts at Freiburg (PD 1911), Munich (PD 1912; ao. Professor 1917), and Tartu (ord. Professor of IE linguistics 1921–1938).

Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the University of Giessen (~1801–1803), he held posts at Giessen (~1808–1816), Göttingen (~1816–1819), and the University of Bonn (~1819–1868).

Haag was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Zurich, Göttingen, and Berlin under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler and Albrecht Weber. He taught at schools in Frauenfeld, Tallinn, Schaffhausen, and Burgdorf, and held posts at Zurich (1873–1884) and Bern (1887–1914).

Friedrich Heiler studied religious studies and Buddhist studies at Munich under Hommel, Dyroff, Kieckers, Kuhn, and Scherman. He held posts at Munich (1918, 1962), Greifswald (1934), Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962), and Marburg (1920–1962).

Friedrich Hirth was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Greifswald, and Rostock. He served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) and held the Dean Lung Professorship at Columbia University (1902–1917).

Friedrich Karl Ginzel was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held an assistant post at the Sternwarte von Oppolzer from 1877 to 1886 and joined the Astronomisches Rechen-Institut in 1886.

Friedrich Karl Slotty studied linguistics and Indology at Greifswald, Breslau, and Jena, studying under Carl Cappeller and Berthold Delbrück. He held posts at Jena (1912, 1919, 1953–1954), Charles University (1925), and the German University in Prague (1928–1939).

Friedrich Kluge was a linguist who studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Strasbourg under August Leskien, Georg Curtius, and Heinrich Hübschmann. He held posts at Strasbourg (1880), the University of Jena (1884, 1886), and the University of Freiburg (1893).

Indologist Friedrich Knauer studied at Tartu, Jena, and Tübingen under Leo Meyer, Leopold von Schroeder, Berthold Delbrück, Carl Cappeller, and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Tartu (1884) and Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv (1886–1914).

Friedrich Kurschat was a linguist who studied at the University of Königsberg from approximately 1836 to 1840. He subsequently held a post at the University of Königsberg from approximately 1841 to 1883.

Friedrich Leberecht Wilhelm Schwartz was a scholar in linguistics, religious studies, and other fields. He completed his studies at the University of Leipzig (~1839–1841) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1841–1844).

Linguist Friedrich Leo studied at Göttingen (~1868–1869) and Bonn (~1869–1873) under Hermann Usener. He held posts at the universities of Bonn (1877–1881), Kiel (1881–1883), Rostock (1883–1888), Strasbourg (1888–1889), and Göttingen (1889–1914).
Friedrich Lorentz was a linguist who pursued his Ph.D. studies at the University of Leipzig from approximately 1890 to 1894 under the instruction of Karl Brugmann and August Leskien.

Friedrich Majer worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied law at the University of Jena in 1791 and studied under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1794–1803), later serving as a Privatdozent at the University of Jena (~1800–1802).
